records.name: ABAP
records.summary: ABAP combines procedural and object-oriented programming on SAP application servers, with language features for database access and business application logic.

records.name: AIDL
records.summary: Android Interface Definition Language describes interfaces whose generated bindings let Android components call one another across process boundaries.

records.name: APL
records.summary: APL is an array-oriented language whose functions and operators express computations over whole collections; Dyalog supplies an interactive implementation.

records.name: ATS
records.summary: ATS combines implementation with formal specification through dependent and linear types, supporting native low-level code alongside theorem-proving constructs.

records.name: ActionScript
records.summary: ActionScript 3 is an object-oriented scripting language supported by Apache Royale, which compiles application code for browser and other targets.
records.lifecycleNote: Apache Royale documents ActionScript 3 support and its December 2024 release.

records.name: Ada
records.summary: Ada is a strongly typed language with explicit interfaces, tasking and contracts, used in embedded and other software where predictable structure matters.
records.lifecycleNote: GCC ships an Ada front end; its supported 16.2 compiler release was published on 7 August 2026.

records.name: Agda
records.summary: Agda uses dependent types to express program properties in types and also serves as an interactive proof assistant for constructive mathematics.
records.lifecycleNote: Agda 2 published v2.8.0.2 on 2026-09-13.

records.name: Aiken
records.summary: Aiken is a statically typed functional language and toolkit for Cardano smart contracts, compiling on-chain validators to Untyped Plutus Core.
records.lifecycleNote: Aiken compiler published v1.1.24 on 2026-09-26.

records.name: Alloy
records.summary: Alloy describes software models using relations and logic; its analyzer searches for examples and counterexamples, including models with changing state.
records.lifecycleNote: The Alloy Analyzer project lists the January 2025 Alloy 6.2.0 release.

records.name: AngelScript
records.summary: AngelScript embeds a statically typed, C/C++-style scripting language in host applications, exposing registered native functions and objects to scripts.
records.lifecycleNote: The AngelScript implementation lists version 2.38.0 released in August 2025.

records.name: Apex
records.summary: Apex runs typed, object-oriented business logic on Salesforce servers, including classes and triggers invoked by record changes and service requests.

records.name: AppleScript
records.summary: AppleScript controls scriptable macOS applications and operating-system features, allowing scripts to combine application actions into repeatable workflows.

records.name: Arc
records.summary: Arc is a Lisp dialect designed around concise expressions and bottom-up programming, where programmers extend the language to fit their application.

records.name: AspectJ
records.summary: AspectJ extends Java with aspect-oriented constructs that express behavior across multiple program locations, such as advice attached to selected join points.

records.name: Assembly
records.summary: Assembly is a family of architecture-specific languages expressing processor instructions, registers and memory operations; syntax depends on the chosen assembler.

records.name: AutoHotkey
records.summary: AutoHotkey is a Windows scripting language for hotkeys, macros and desktop automation, with scripts that interact with keyboard input and application windows.
records.lifecycleNote: AutoHotkey v2 published v2.0.30 on 2026-10-09.

records.name: AutoIt
records.summary: AutoIt uses BASIC-like syntax to automate Windows interfaces and general tasks, including keystrokes, controls, COM objects and calls to native libraries.
records.lifecycleNote: AutoIt v3 lists version 3.3.18.0 released on 2025-09-07.

records.name: Awk
records.summary: Awk processes input records through pattern-action rules, combining regular-expression matching, fields, arrays and output formatting for text-oriented tasks.

records.name: BASIC
records.summary: BASIC began at Dartmouth in 1964 to make programming accessible to students through time-sharing. Later BASIC dialects have different syntax and runtimes; FreeBASIC and Visual Basic .NET have separate profiles.

records.name: BQN
records.summary: BQN is an array-oriented language in the APL tradition, combining multidimensional array operations, higher-order functions and a distinct symbolic notation.

records.name: Ballerina
records.summary: Ballerina is designed for service integration, with network-oriented language constructs and tools for building APIs and connecting distributed systems.
records.lifecycleNote: Ballerina distribution published v2201.13.7 on 2026-10-08.

records.name: Bash
records.summary: Bash is GNU's Bourne-compatible command shell, combining interactive command editing and job control with functions, arrays and scripts for automating shell tasks.
records.lifecycleNote: GNU identifies a current Bash maintainer and an active development and bug-reporting process.

records.name: Bicep
records.summary: Bicep declaratively describes Azure resources and their relationships, compiling infrastructure definitions into Azure Resource Manager deployment templates.
records.lifecycleNote: Microsoft Bicep compiler published v0.48.1 on 2026-10-05.

records.name: Bison
records.summary: Bison grammar files describe tokens, grammar rules and semantic actions from which GNU Bison generates parsers for programming languages and other structured inputs.

records.name: BlitzMax
records.summary: BlitzMax provides a cross-platform programming language and modular toolchain, with libraries ranging from game frameworks to database connectivity.
records.lifecycleNote: BlitzMax NG published v0.165.3.61.linux.x64 on 2026-08-24.

records.name: Bluespec
records.summary: Bluespec describes digital hardware through typed modules and guarded atomic actions; the BSC toolchain can simulate designs and generate standard Verilog.
records.lifecycleNote: Bluespec Compiler (BSC) published 2026.07.1 on 2026-09-26.

records.name: Boo
records.summary: Boo is a programming language for the .NET runtime whose compiler produces .NET assemblies and whose interpreter runs scripts from files or standard input.

records.name: Boogie
records.summary: Boogie is an intermediate verification language separating source-language translation from the back-end reasoning used to check program correctness.
records.lifecycleNote: Boogie verifier published v3.5.8 on 2026-10-03.

records.name: C
records.summary: C developed alongside Unix in the early 1970s. It provides procedural programming, explicit pointers and storage control for native programs and libraries.

links.label: Ritchie: C development, 1969–1973; central work in 1972

records.lifecycleNote: GCC ships a C front end; its supported 16.2 compiler release was published on 7 August 2026.

records.name: C#
records.summary: C# is a statically typed language for .NET with classes, value types, generics and automatic memory management. Its libraries cover web services, desktop software and other application workloads.
records.lifecycleNote: C# ships in the .NET SDK; Microsoft's September 2026 support table lists .NET 10 as actively supported.

records.name: C++
records.summary: C++ extends the C tradition with classes, templates, deterministic object lifetimes and a standard library for constructing native applications and reusable abstractions.

links.label: Stroustrup: first use under the C++ name in 1983

records.lifecycleNote: GCC ships a C++ front end; its supported 16.2 compiler release was published on 7 August 2026.

records.name: C3
records.summary: C3 develops C-style syntax and semantics into a general-purpose compiled language aimed at systems code, applications, games and developer tools.
records.lifecycleNote: C3 compiler published v0.8.5 on 2026-10-10.

records.name: CLIPS
records.summary: CLIPS is a rule-based programming language for expert systems, combining facts and production rules to express heuristic decision logic.

records.name: CMake
records.summary: The CMake language expresses build specifications and reusable modules in CMakeLists.txt and .cmake files, and also supports standalone command scripts.

records.name: COBOL
records.summary: COBOL was developed for business data processing and uses record-oriented, English-like program structure. Existing applications include financial, administrative and mainframe systems.
records.lifecycleNote: GCC lists a COBOL front end and a supported 16.2 compiler release from 7 August 2026; this describes that implementation.

records.name: Cairo
records.summary: Cairo expresses programs whose execution can be proved using validity proofs and serves as the smart-contract language for the Starknet blockchain.
records.lifecycleNote: Cairo compiler published v2.21.0 on 2026-10-09.

records.name: Carbon
records.summary: Carbon is an experimental successor-language project for C++, exploring interoperability and migration while its compiler and language design remain in development.
records.lifecycleNote: The Carbon project explicitly describes its language and toolchain as experimental.

records.name: Ceylon
records.summary: Ceylon has a type-checking compiler, module system and Java and JavaScript back ends; the Eclipse project covering these tools is officially archived.
records.lifecycleNote: The Eclipse Ceylon language and toolchain project is explicitly archived.

records.name: Chapel
records.summary: Chapel is a compiled language built around parallel computation, with constructs for expressing algorithms across cores and distributed computing resources.
records.lifecycleNote: Chapel compiler published 2.10.0 on 2026-09-24.

records.name: Circom
records.summary: Circom describes arithmetic circuits using signals, constraints and reusable templates; its compiler produces representations used to build zero-knowledge proofs.
records.lifecycleNote: Circom 2 compiler published v2.2.3 on 2025-10-27.

records.name: Clarion
records.summary: Clarion builds database-oriented applications using a data dictionary, code-generation templates and a programming language for application-specific behavior.

records.name: Clean
records.summary: Clean is a pure, lazy functional language with uniqueness typing, dynamic types and generic functions; its ecosystem includes workflow and embedded-device frameworks.

records.name: Clojure
records.summary: Clojure is a dynamic Lisp hosted on the JVM, using persistent immutable collections, macros and explicit state-management mechanisms for functional and concurrent programs.
records.lifecycleNote: The official Clojure site reports release 1.12.6 on 2 September 2026 and continuing 1.13 development.

records.name: CoffeeScript
records.summary: CoffeeScript compiles a compact alternative syntax into JavaScript, including classes, comprehensions and functions that interoperate with JavaScript libraries.

records.name: Common Lisp
records.summary: Common Lisp supports interactive development, functions, macros and objects; implementations such as SBCL provide an ANSI Common Lisp compiler and runtime.
records.lifecycleNote: SBCL lists version 2.6.9 released in September 2026.

records.name: Component Pascal
records.summary: Component Pascal is an Oberon-2-derived language used by the BlackBox Component Builder, which combines a development environment with a modular application framework.

records.name: Crystal
records.summary: Crystal is a compiled, statically checked language with Ruby-inspired syntax and type inference, supporting native libraries, fibers and channels.
records.lifecycleNote: Crystal compiler published 1.21.1 on 2026-09-26.

records.name: Cuda
records.summary: CUDA C++ extends C++ with GPU kernels and launch syntax, expressing parallel work using NVIDIA's thread, block and memory programming model.

records.name: Curry
records.summary: Curry combines lazy functional programming with logic variables, search and nondeterministic operations in a declarative language with static types.

records.name: Cypher
records.summary: Cypher is a declarative query language for property graph databases, expressing searches and transformations in terms of nodes, relationships and patterns.
records.lifecycleNote: Neo4j documents new Cypher 25 features from 2025 and its database default from February 2026.

records.name: Cython
records.summary: Cython extends Python-oriented code with static declarations and native C/C++ interoperability, compiling modules that integrate with the CPython ecosystem.
records.lifecycleNote: Cython compiler published 3.3.0 on 2026-08-22.

records.name: D
records.summary: D is a statically typed general-purpose language with C-like syntax, systems-level access and native compilation, supporting both high-level abstractions and low-level code.
records.lifecycleNote: The D compiler release chronology lists implementation releases in 2026.

records.name: Dafny
records.summary: Dafny combines executable programs with specifications and a static verifier, checking properties expressed through contracts, invariants and mathematical reasoning.
records.lifecycleNote: Dafny verifier and compiler published v4.11.0 on 2025-08-25.

records.name: Dart
records.summary: Dart is a type-safe language that powers Flutter and supports web and native compilation. Its language and runtimes focus on client applications across mobile, desktop and browser targets.
records.lifecycleNote: The Dart team documents the 3.13 SDK release on 12 August 2026.

records.name: Dhall
records.summary: Dhall is a typed configuration language with functions and imports that evaluates to ordinary configuration data while restricting arbitrary side effects.
records.lifecycleNote: Dhall Haskell implementation published 1.42.2 on 2025-01-19.

records.name: Dylan
records.summary: Dylan is an object-functional language descended from Scheme and CLOS, using non-Lisp syntax and a programming model supporting native machine-code generation.
records.lifecycleNote: Open Dylan published v2026.2.0 on 2026-07-10.

records.name: Eiffel
records.summary: Eiffel is an object-oriented language and development approach centered on classes, inheritance and Design by Contract for specifying software obligations.

records.name: Elixir
records.summary: Elixir builds on Erlang's runtime with immutable data, lightweight processes and message passing. Its ecosystem includes real-time web applications, distributed services and embedded projects.
records.lifecycleNote: The Elixir implementation published version 1.20.4 on 28 August 2026.

records.name: Elm
records.summary: Elm is a statically typed functional language that compiles to JavaScript, using a model, messages and update functions to construct browser user interfaces.

records.name: Emacs Lisp
records.summary: Emacs Lisp is the Lisp dialect embedded in GNU Emacs, providing language constructs and editor-specific operations for customization and extension packages.

records.name: Erlang
records.summary: Erlang is a functional language with lightweight processes, messaging and distributed runtime support. OTP adds libraries and design patterns for fault-tolerant networked systems.
records.lifecycleNote: The Erlang/OTP team announced the 29.1 maintenance release on 16 September 2026.

records.name: F#
records.summary: F# is a .NET language combining functional, object-oriented and imperative programming, with pattern matching, type inference and access to .NET libraries.
records.lifecycleNote: Microsoft .NET F# implementation published v13.9.201 on 2025-02-11.

records.name: F*
records.summary: F* is a proof-oriented functional language with dependent and refinement types; verified code can be extracted through its toolchains to other implementation languages.
records.lifecycleNote: The F* project explicitly reports active development by Microsoft Research, Inria and its community.

records.name: Factor
records.summary: Factor is a stack-based, concatenative language with an interactive development environment, where composing words builds programs from operations on the data stack.
records.lifecycleNote: The Factor implementation lists development builds dated October 2026.

records.name: Fantom
records.summary: Fantom runs on the JVM and in browsers, combining Java-like syntax with static and dynamic typing, closures, immutability and actor-style concurrency.
records.lifecycleNote: Fantom distribution published v1.0.83 on 2026-03-12.

records.name: Faust
records.summary: Faust is a functional language for digital signal processing that describes audio computations and compiles them for a variety of audio applications and platforms.
records.lifecycleNote: Faust compiler published 2.88.0 on 2026-09-09.

records.name: Fennel
records.summary: Fennel brings Lisp-style syntax and macros to Lua, compiling to Lua code that can use Lua libraries and existing Lua application runtimes.

records.name: Flix
records.summary: Flix combines typed functional programming with effect tracking, pattern matching and structured concurrency, supported by a whole-program optimizing compiler.
records.lifecycleNote: The Flix project explicitly describes its compiler as actively developed and maintained.

records.name: Forth
records.summary: Forth is a stack-based language and interactive programming environment whose extensible vocabulary of words supports application and low-level development.

records.name: Fortran
records.summary: Fortran is a statically typed language designed for numerical work, with array operations and language support for parallel computation in scientific programs.
records.lifecycleNote: GCC ships a Fortran front end; its supported 16.2 compiler release was published on 7 August 2026.

records.name: FreeBASIC
records.summary: FreeBASIC compiles BASIC programs for Windows, DOS and Linux; its QB mode supports many QuickBASIC programs, while its default mode offers a different language dialect.

records.name: Frege
records.summary: Frege brings a Haskell-style, purely functional language to the JVM, allowing functional programs to run on the Java platform and interoperate with Java code.

records.name: Futhark
records.summary: Futhark is a purely functional, data-parallel array language whose compiler transforms high-level array computations into code for parallel execution.
records.lifecycleNote: Futhark compiler published v0.28.1 on 2026-10-11.

records.name: GAMS
records.summary: GAMS describes mathematical optimization problems using sets, parameters, variables and equations, then connects the resulting models to selected solvers.
records.lifecycleNote: GAMS lists the September 2026 54.5.0 release in its documentation center.

records.name: GAP
records.summary: GAP provides a programming language and libraries for computational discrete algebra, with a particular focus on group-theoretic computations.
records.lifecycleNote: GAP system published v4.16.1 on 2026-08-23.

records.name: GDScript
records.summary: GDScript is an indentation-based, gradually typed language built specifically for Godot, integrating object-oriented scripts with the engine's game objects and tools.

records.name: GLSL
records.summary: GLSL is OpenGL's shading language for programmable graphics stages, expressing operations that run as shaders rather than ordinary CPU application code.

records.name: Gherkin
records.summary: Gherkin describes behavior examples as structured scenarios with Given, When and Then steps; Cucumber connects those steps to executable test definitions.

records.name: Gleam
records.summary: Gleam is a typed functional language that runs on the Erlang virtual machine and also compiles to JavaScript, interoperating with Erlang and Elixir packages.
records.lifecycleNote: Gleam compiler published v1.19.1 on 2026-10-07.

records.name: Gnuplot
records.summary: Gnuplot scripts describe plots of functions and data using commands such as plot and splot, producing two-dimensional charts and three-dimensional views.
records.lifecycleNote: The gnuplot implementation lists version 6.0.5 released in July 2026.

records.name: Go
records.summary: Go is a statically typed language that compiles to machine code and includes garbage collection, goroutines and channels, with standard libraries for networking and application tooling.
records.lifecycleNote: The Go project reports Go 1.27.2, including security and runtime fixes, on 8 October 2026.

records.name: Gosu
records.summary: Gosu is a typed JVM language with Java interoperability, an open type system, extension methods, structural typing and script-style program files.

records.name: Groovy
records.summary: Groovy is a Java-like JVM language supporting static and dynamic typing, closures and metaprogramming, with direct interoperability with Java libraries.

records.name: HCL
records.summary: HashiCorp Configuration Language provides blocks, attributes and expressions for structured configuration; tools such as Terraform define their own semantics on top.
records.lifecycleNote: HashiCorp HCL implementation published v2.25.0 on 2026-09-15.

records.name: HLSL
records.summary: HLSL is a C-like shader language for DirectX, used to write graphics pipeline stages and compute shaders executed by programmable GPU hardware.
records.lifecycleNote: Microsoft DirectX Shader Compiler published v1.9.2609 on 2026-09-29.

records.name: Hack
records.summary: Hack is an object-oriented language built for the HHVM runtime, using static type checking, generics and asynchronous operations for web applications.
records.lifecycleNote: The Hack project explicitly states that Hack and HHVM are in active development with frequent releases.

records.name: Hare
records.summary: Hare is a statically typed systems language with manual memory management and a minimal runtime, intended for system tools and other low-level software.
records.lifecycleNote: The Hare toolchain lists version 0.26.0 released in February 2026.

records.name: Haskell
records.summary: Haskell is a purely functional language with lazy evaluation, immutable values and a strong type system, using functions and algebraic data types to model programs.

records.name: Haxe
records.summary: Haxe is a strictly typed language with a cross-compiler targeting platforms such as JavaScript, C++, JVM and Lua, supporting shared code across application targets.
records.lifecycleNote: The Haxe compiler lists version 4.3.7 released in May 2025 and a 5.0 preview from July 2025.

records.name: Hy
records.summary: Hy is a Lisp dialect embedded in Python, providing alternative syntax and Lisp features while retaining direct access to Python built-ins and third-party libraries.
records.lifecycleNote: Hy implementation published 1.3.1 on 2026-07-31.

records.name: Idris
records.summary: Idris supports type-driven development with first-class types, allowing types to express relationships between values and to guide construction of programs and proofs.
records.lifecycleNote: Idris 2 published v0.8.0 on 2025-10-31.

records.name: Imba
records.summary: Imba compiles to JavaScript and integrates DOM tags and styling into its syntax for building browser interfaces and Node.js applications.

records.name: Inform 7
records.summary: Inform 7 describes interactive-fiction worlds and rules using natural-language-style source text, supporting stories, narrative prototypes and teaching.

records.name: Io
records.summary: Io is a prototype-based dynamic language in which expressions are messages and objects are cloned; its VM can be embedded in WebAssembly hosts.
records.lifecycleNote: The Io project documents its VM and WASM/WASI implementation update dated 2026-04-20.

records.name: J
records.summary: J is an array-oriented general-purpose language whose operations work on whole arrays, with an interactive environment for mathematical and data-oriented programs.
records.lifecycleNote: J compiler implementation released build96 on 2025-03-06.

records.name: JSONiq
records.summary: JSONiq is a query language for selecting, aggregating and transforming JSON data, with implementations such as RumbleDB for local and distributed processing.
records.lifecycleNote: The language's official site identifies RumbleDB as its fully supported recommended implementation.

records.name: Jai
records.summary: Jai is Jonathan Blow's programming-language project for game development, with compiler design and language features demonstrated in the creator's presentations.

records.name: Janet
records.summary: Janet combines functional and imperative programming in an embeddable runtime, with closures, macros and facilities for system scripting.
records.lifecycleNote: Janet implementation released v1.42.1 on 2026-09-11.

records.name: Java
records.summary: Java is a statically typed, object-oriented language supported by the Java virtual machine and extensive standard APIs, including collections, concurrency and networked application facilities.
records.lifecycleNote: OpenJDK's JDK 27 reference implementation reached general availability on 15 September 2026.

records.name: JavaScript
records.summary: JavaScript is a dynamically typed language with prototype-based objects and first-class functions. Browsers expose DOM APIs, while runtimes such as Node.js provide server and file-system facilities.
records.lifecycleNote: Node.js reports current v26 releases and supported v24/v22 LTS branches, with updates in September and October 2026.

records.name: Jolie
records.summary: Jolie models services, message interfaces and orchestration workflows directly in the language, with communication that can use different network protocols.
records.lifecycleNote: Jolie implementation released v1.12.8 on 2026-03-01.

records.name: Jsonnet
records.summary: Jsonnet extends JSON with functions, variables and object composition, producing configuration data without side effects rather than executing deployment actions.
records.lifecycleNote: Jsonnet implementation released v0.22.0 on 2026-03-24.

records.name: Julia
records.summary: Julia is a dynamically typed language built around multiple dispatch and native-code compilation, with interactive tooling and libraries for numerical, scientific and general application work.
records.lifecycleNote: The Julia implementation published version 1.13.1 on 26 September 2026.

records.name: KCL
records.summary: KCL is a schema-based configuration language for defining data structures, validating configuration and generating infrastructure configuration from reusable models.
records.lifecycleNote: KCL implementation released v0.13.1 on 2026-10-07.

records.name: Koka
records.summary: Koka is a statically typed functional language whose effect types and handlers describe operations such as state, exceptions and asynchronous computations.
records.lifecycleNote: The Koka project explicitly describes v3 as a research language under development and not ready for production use.

records.name: Kotlin
records.summary: Kotlin is a programming language with Java interoperability and multiplatform tooling, used for Android applications, server software and shared application code.
records.lifecycleNote: Kotlin implementation released v2.4.21 on 2026-10-08.

records.name: LabVIEW
records.summary: LabVIEW programs use the graphical G language and dataflow diagrams to acquire measurements, control instruments and build automated test systems.
records.lifecycleNote: NI's release-notes index lists LabVIEW 2026 Q3 and 2026 Q1 product releases.

records.name: Lean
records.summary: Lean combines an interactive theorem prover with a dependently typed programming language; its current Lean 4 implementation supports proofs and executable programs.
records.lifecycleNote: Lean 4 implementation released v4.34.1 on 2026-09-24.

records.name: Lean 4
records.summary: Lean 4 reimplements the Lean theorem prover in Lean, combining extensible proof automation with a functional language and native-code compilation.
records.lifecycleNote: Lean 4 implementation released v4.34.1 on 2026-09-24.

records.name: LilyPond
records.summary: LilyPond turns a text-based music notation language into engraved scores, supporting orchestral parts, tablature and other structured notation.
records.lifecycleNote: The LilyPond project announced stable 2.26.0 on 2026-04-21 and development 2.27.3 on 2026-09-10.

records.name: LiveScript
records.summary: LiveScript compiles to JavaScript and adds features such as pattern matching, comprehensions and concise functions for functional and imperative programming.

records.name: Logtalk
records.summary: Logtalk extends Prolog with objects, protocols and reusable categories, organising declarative logic programs while using Prolog implementations as backends.
records.lifecycleNote: The Logtalk project published release 3.102.0 on 2026-09-14.

records.name: Lua
records.summary: Lua is an embeddable, dynamically typed scripting language with table-based data structures and bytecode execution, often used to configure or extend a host application.
records.lifecycleNote: PUC-Rio's Lua team explicitly identifies itself as the language's designers, implementers and maintainers; its page was updated in October 2026.

records.name: Luau
records.summary: Luau extends Lua-style scripting with gradual types and an embeddable runtime, supporting host-controlled application scripting and Roblox development.
records.lifecycleNote: Luau implementation released 0.742 on 2026-10-10.

records.name: MATLAB
records.summary: MATLAB is a language and numeric computing environment for developing algorithms, analysing data and visualising results in engineering and science.
records.lifecycleNote: MathWorks announced MATLAB R2026b released on 2026-09-23.

records.name: MQL4
records.summary: MQL4 is MetaTrader 4's language for Expert Advisors, scripts and custom indicators, giving programs access to market quotes and trading-order operations.

records.name: MQL5
records.summary: MQL5 is MetaTrader 5's C++-style language for trading robots, technical indicators and utility programs that interact with the trading platform.

records.name: Mercury
records.summary: Mercury combines logic and functional programming with static types, modes and determinism checking to build modular declarative applications.
records.lifecycleNote: The Mercury project announced compiler release 22.01.9 on 2026-08-30.

records.name: Metal
records.summary: Metal's shading language defines GPU graphics and compute functions for Apple's Metal API, covering rendering shaders and parallel computation on Apple platforms.

records.name: MiniZinc
records.summary: MiniZinc is a high-level constraint modelling language for expressing discrete optimisation problems independently of the particular solver used to solve them.
records.lifecycleNote: MiniZinc implementation released 2.10.1 on 2026-08-31.

records.name: Modelica
records.summary: Modelica describes physical systems with mathematical equations and reusable connected components, supporting simulations of mechanical, electrical and other systems.

records.name: Modula-2
records.summary: Modula-2 separates interfaces from implementation in modules and includes facilities for systems programming; GNU Modula-2 supports PIM and ISO dialects.

records.name: Modula-3
records.summary: Modula-3 is a modular systems language with objects, exceptions, threads and garbage collection, implemented by the Critical Mass Modula-3 toolchain.
records.lifecycleNote: Critical Mass Modula-3 implementation released d5.12.0 on 2026-03-27.

records.name: Mojo
records.summary: Mojo is a systems programming language for CPU and GPU code, combining readable syntax with memory management controls and compile-time metaprogramming.
records.lifecycleNote: The Mojo project lists stable 1.1.0 dated September 17 and a nightly dated October 9 on its current release page.

records.name: MoonBit
records.summary: MoonBit is a statically typed general-purpose language and toolchain with native and WebAssembly targets, algebraic data types and pattern matching.
records.lifecycleNote: The MoonBit project announced moonc compiler v0.10.14 on 2026-09-21.

records.name: MoonScript
records.summary: MoonScript is a dynamic language with indentation-based syntax and classes that compiles to Lua, allowing existing Lua libraries and hosts to be reused.
records.lifecycleNote: MoonScript implementation released v0.7.0 on 2026-07-26.

records.name: Motoko
records.summary: Motoko is a language for Internet Computer canister applications, with actors, asynchronous calls and persistent data integrated into its programming model.
records.lifecycleNote: Motoko implementation released 2.0.0 on 2026-10-06.

records.name: Move
records.summary: Move represents assets as resources with controlled ownership and transfer, providing modules and transaction logic for blockchain applications.

records.name: Nemerle
records.summary: Nemerle is a statically typed .NET language combining functional, object-oriented and imperative code with macros for extending compilation and embedding DSLs.

records.name: Nextflow
records.summary: Nextflow expresses computational workflows as processes connected by dataflow channels, running pipelines across local, cluster and cloud execution environments.
records.lifecycleNote: Nextflow implementation released v26.04.7 on 2026-10-08.

records.name: Nim
records.summary: Nim is a statically typed compiled language with indentation-based syntax and compile-time macros. Its back ends produce C, C++ or JavaScript for native and browser applications.
records.lifecycleNote: The Nim team announced stable compiler version 2.2.12 on 8 September 2026.

records.name: Nix
records.summary: Nix is a lazy functional language for describing packages and configurations, used by the Nix tools to evaluate build recipes and development environments.

records.name: Nushell
records.summary: Nushell is a cross-platform shell language whose pipelines carry structured values and tables, supporting data transformation and system automation.
records.lifecycleNote: Nushell implementation released 0.116.1 on 2026-10-04.

records.name: OCaml
records.summary: OCaml is a statically typed functional language with pattern matching, modules and garbage collection, offering both native and bytecode compilation for application and language-tool development.
records.lifecycleNote: The OCaml project reports compiler version 5.5.1 on 5 September 2026 and an available 4.14 LTS series.

records.name: Oberon
records.summary: Oberon is a compact modular language developed with the Oberon operating system, extending Pascal-style records to support extensible systems and applications.

records.name: Objective-C
records.summary: Objective-C adds object-oriented messaging to C and is used by existing Cocoa applications. Its APIs and language conventions connect C code to the Objective-C runtime.
records.lifecycleNote: GCC lists an Objective-C front end and a supported 16.2 compiler release from 7 August 2026; this does not describe Apple's SDK lifecycle.

records.name: Objective-J
records.summary: Objective-J extends JavaScript with Objective-C-style classes and message syntax, and is used with Cappuccino to build desktop-style applications in the browser.

records.name: Odin
records.summary: Odin is a compiled general-purpose language focused on systems and data-oriented programming, with explicit memory allocators and support for array operations.
records.lifecycleNote: Odin implementation released dev-2026-10 on 2026-10-06.

records.name: OpenCL
records.summary: OpenCL provides a kernel programming language and APIs for running parallel computations across CPUs, GPUs and other accelerators in heterogeneous systems.

records.name: OpenQASM
records.summary: OpenQASM describes quantum circuits and their classical control flow, acting as an intermediate representation between quantum compilers and hardware.

records.name: OpenSCAD
records.summary: OpenSCAD describes solid 3D objects with scripts and configurable parameters, rendering models from geometric operations rather than interactive drawing.

records.name: Oz
records.summary: Oz is the language implemented by the Mozart programming system, combining declarative computation, concurrency and constraint-oriented programming.
records.lifecycleNote: The Mozart 2 implementation's official repository describes it as alpha quality and not ready for production.

records.name: P4
records.summary: P4 describes packet headers, parsing and forwarding actions for programmable network data planes, with compilers that target particular hardware or software switches.
records.lifecycleNote: p4c implementation released v1.2.5.18 on 2026-10-02.

records.name: PHP
records.summary: PHP executes scripts on the server to generate web responses and also provides a command-line interpreter, with procedural and object-oriented facilities and database extensions.
records.lifecycleNote: The PHP team announced supported-branch security releases, including PHP 8.5.11, on 24 September 2026.

records.name: Pascal
records.summary: Pascal is a structured procedural language originating in Niklaus Wirth's work at ETH, with descendants and compilers supporting applications and programming education.

records.name: Perl
records.summary: Perl is a general-purpose scripting language with regular expressions, text-processing facilities and a large module ecosystem, used in automation, web applications and database integration.

records.name: PicoLisp
records.summary: PicoLisp is a data-oriented Lisp system integrating a language, persistent object database and web interface facilities for building applications.

records.name: Pony
records.summary: Pony is a compiled actor-model language using reference capabilities to govern object sharing and mutation, with asynchronous actors and native C interoperability.
records.lifecycleNote: ponyc implementation released 0.75.0 on 2026-10-11.

records.name: PowerShell
records.summary: PowerShell combines an object-oriented command shell, scripting language and configuration tools. Commands pass structured .NET objects through pipelines for system and cloud automation.
records.lifecycleNote: The PowerShell implementation published version 7.6.6 on 8 September 2026.

records.name: Processing
records.summary: Processing is a programming language and environment for visual arts, using sketch-style programs to create graphics, animation and interactive projects.
records.lifecycleNote: Processing implementation released processing-1435-4.5.7 on 2026-09-24.

records.name: Prolog
records.summary: Prolog expresses relationships as facts and rules and searches for solutions to queries, supporting symbolic reasoning and applications built with logic programming.
records.lifecycleNote: SWI-Prolog implementation released V10.1.17 on 2026-10-04.

records.name: Puppet
records.summary: Puppet's declarative language describes desired resource states in manifests, which the Puppet tools compile and apply to configure machines.
records.lifecycleNote: Puppet Core 9.1.0 documentation was published on 2026-10-06 and documents its supported manifest language.

records.name: PureScript
records.summary: PureScript is a statically typed functional language that compiles to JavaScript, with type inference and an ecosystem for browser and server applications.
records.lifecycleNote: PureScript implementation released v0.15.16 on 2026-03-15.

records.name: Python
records.summary: Python is a dynamically typed language supporting procedural, object-oriented and functional code. Its standard library and package ecosystem serve automation, web development and scientific applications.

links.label: Python FAQ: first public posting in February 1991

records.lifecycleNote: The Python project announced Python 3.15.0 on 9 October 2026 and maintenance releases earlier that month.

records.name: Q#
records.summary: Q# is Microsoft's language for expressing quantum programs in the Quantum Development Kit, including qubit operations and classical control logic.
records.lifecycleNote: Microsoft QDK implementation released v1.33.0 on 2026-10-06.

records.name: R
records.summary: R is a language and environment for statistical computation and graphics, providing data analysis, modelling and extensible plotting facilities with links to native-code libraries.
records.lifecycleNote: The R project announced the R 4.6.1 release on 24 June 2026.

records.name: Racket
records.summary: Racket is a Lisp-family language and platform for language-oriented programming, with macros and tools for creating domain-specific languages and applications.
records.lifecycleNote: Racket implementation released v9.3 on 2026-08-13.

records.name: Raku
records.summary: Raku combines functional, object-oriented and other programming styles with grammars, gradual typing and facilities for scripting and concurrent programs.
records.lifecycleNote: Rakudo implementation released 2026.09 on 2026-09-28.

records.name: ReScript
records.summary: ReScript is a statically typed language that compiles to JavaScript, with JavaScript interoperability and tools for browser, Node.js and React applications.
records.lifecycleNote: ReScript implementation released v12.3.1 on 2026-08-24.

records.name: Reason
records.summary: Reason provides alternative syntax and tooling for OCaml, retaining its type system and allowing native OCaml applications or JavaScript output through Melange.
records.lifecycleNote: Reason tooling implementation released 3.18.0 on 2026-06-23.

records.name: Red
records.summary: Red is a Rebol-inspired language and toolchain with built-in dialects for parsing, GUI layout and lower-level programming, combining interpreted and compiled code.
records.lifecycleNote: The Red toolchain's official repository explicitly describes its current development stage as alpha.

records.name: Ring
records.summary: Ring is a dynamic multi-paradigm language with support for embedded domain-specific syntax and libraries for console, graphical, web and mobile applications.
records.lifecycleNote: Ring implementation released v1.27 on 2026-05-28.

records.name: Roc
records.summary: Roc is a statically typed functional language that separates application code from platform code, using type inference and platform packages for host integration.

records.name: Ruby
records.summary: Ruby is a dynamic object-oriented language with blocks and metaprogramming, used for scripting, data processing and web applications with frameworks such as Rails.
records.lifecycleNote: The Ruby project released Ruby 4.0.7 on 2026-09-15.

records.name: Rust
records.summary: Rust is a compiled systems language whose ownership and borrowing rules govern memory use and sharing, with applications in services, command-line tools and embedded code.
records.lifecycleNote: The Rust Release Team announced Rust 1.99.0 on 2026-10-01.

records.name: SAS
records.summary: SAS programs combine DATA steps for managing data with procedures for analysis and reporting, and macros for generating and reusing program text.
records.lifecycleNote: SAS announced SAS 9.4M9 in June 2025 with Standard Support through July 2030.

records.name: Scala
records.summary: Scala combines object-oriented and functional programming with static types, pattern matching and metaprogramming, supporting applications that integrate with its host platforms and libraries.
records.lifecycleNote: The Scala 3 implementation published compiler version 3.10.0 on 12 October 2026.

records.name: Scheme
records.summary: Scheme is a Lisp-family language emphasising lexical scope, first-class procedures and a compact core, with several independently developed implementations.

records.name: Smalltalk
records.summary: Smalltalk organises computation as objects exchanging messages, with live environments such as Squeak that let developers inspect and change running programs.
records.lifecycleNote: The OpenSmalltalk VM used by Squeak and Cuis published release 202606270913 on 2026-06-27.

records.name: Solidity
records.summary: Solidity is a statically typed language for smart contracts targeting the Ethereum Virtual Machine, with inheritance, libraries and user-defined types for on-chain application logic.
records.lifecycleNote: The Solidity compiler implementation published version 0.8.37 on 10 September 2026.

records.name: Squirrel
records.summary: Squirrel is a dynamic object-oriented language designed for embedding in applications such as games, with classes, generators and cooperative coroutines.

records.name: Standard ML
records.summary: Standard ML is a functional language with type inference, algebraic data types and modules; its formal definition specifies both typing and execution semantics.
records.lifecycleNote: The SML/NJ implementation published development release 2026.2 on 2026-08-14.

records.name: Starlark
records.summary: Starlark is a Python-like embedded configuration language with deterministic evaluation, used for Bazel build definitions and application-specific extension logic.
records.lifecycleNote: Bazel, which embeds Starlark for build rules, released 9.3.0 on 2026-10-07.

records.name: SuperCollider
records.summary: SuperCollider's sclang language controls a separate real-time audio server, supporting algorithmic sound synthesis, composition and interactive musical systems.
records.lifecycleNote: SuperCollider implementation released Version-3.14.1 on 2025-11-24.

records.name: Swift
records.summary: Swift is a statically typed language with value types, generics and optionals, used for applications on Apple platforms and for services and tooling on other supported platforms.
records.lifecycleNote: The Swift implementation published its 6.4.0 release on 15 September 2026.

records.name: TLA
records.summary: TLA+ is a mathematical specification language for describing state transitions and checking models of software or hardware, especially concurrent and distributed systems.

records.name: Tcl
records.summary: Tcl is an extensible dynamic scripting language used for automation, networking and application integration; its companion Tk toolkit supplies graphical interfaces.
records.lifecycleNote: The Tcl/Tk project lists Tcl/Tk 9.1.0 released on 2026-09-29.

records.name: Terra
records.summary: Terra is a compiled low-level language embedded in Lua, allowing Lua programs to generate and specialise native code and embed domain-specific JIT compilers.
records.lifecycleNote: Terra implementation released release-1.2.2 on 2026-08-14.

records.name: TypeScript
records.summary: TypeScript adds static type annotations and checking to JavaScript, then emits JavaScript that runs in browsers and server runtimes.
records.lifecycleNote: TypeScript implementation released v7.0.2 on 2026-08-20.

records.name: V
records.summary: V is a compiled language with C interoperability and integrated tooling, supporting native applications, command-line programs and network services.
records.lifecycleNote: V implementation released 0.5.2 on 2026-07-12.

records.name: VBA
records.summary: Visual Basic for Applications is embedded in Microsoft Office applications, using their object models to automate documents, spreadsheets and other repeated tasks.

records.name: VBScript
records.summary: VBScript is Microsoft's Visual Basic-family scripting language used with Windows Script Host and legacy Windows applications; Microsoft is phasing out its Windows component.
records.lifecycleNote: Microsoft deprecated the Windows VBScript component in October 2023 and plans phased removal; existing installations can still run it.

records.name: VHDL
records.summary: VHDL describes hardware designs whose behaviour can be simulated and whose synthesizable portions can be translated into gate-level implementations.
records.lifecycleNote: GHDL implementation released v6.0.0 on 2026-03-07.

records.name: Vala
records.summary: Vala offers object-oriented syntax and native compilation with direct GObject and GTK support, allowing applications to use existing C libraries.
records.lifecycleNote: GNOME published the Vala compiler 0.56.19 source release on 2026-03-30.

records.name: Verilog
records.summary: Verilog is a hardware description language for modelling digital circuits, writing simulation testbenches and describing designs for logic synthesis.
records.lifecycleNote: Icarus Verilog implementation released v13_0 on 2026-03-02.

records.name: Visual Basic .NET
records.summary: Visual Basic .NET is a .NET language with a stable design, used for Windows Forms applications and libraries. Microsoft's strategy retains core library support and C# interoperability without expanding to new workloads.
records.lifecycleNote: Microsoft's current strategy retains .NET library support and Visual Studio investment for existing Visual Basic scenarios; the language design remains stable.

records.name: WebAssembly
records.summary: WebAssembly is a binary instruction format for a stack-based virtual machine, serving as a portable compilation target for programs deployed in host environments.

records.name: Wolfram Language
records.summary: Wolfram Language represents code and data as symbolic expressions and includes built-in computation and visualisation functions for technical and mathematical work.
records.lifecycleNote: The Mathematica implementation released version 15 in June 2026 and 15.0.1 with fixes in July 2026.

records.name: XQuery
records.summary: XQuery is a W3C query language for selecting and constructing XML data; XQuery 3.1 also adds maps, arrays and operations for working with JSON.

records.name: Xtend
records.summary: Xtend is a statically typed Java dialect that generates readable Java source, adding features such as lambdas, extension methods and compile-time macros.

records.name: Yacc
records.summary: Yacc uses grammar rules and associated actions to generate parsers, traditionally producing C source for recognising structured input such as programming-language syntax.

records.name: Yul
records.summary: Yul is Solidity's intermediate language for optimisation and EVM bytecode generation, and can also be written directly as Solidity inline assembly.
records.lifecycleNote: Solidity implementation released v0.8.37 on 2026-09-10.

records.name: Zeek
records.summary: Zeek's event-driven scripting language extends its network monitor, turning protocol events into custom analysis, logs and network-observation policies.
records.lifecycleNote: Zeek implementation released v9.0.0 on 2026-08-21.

records.name: Zig
records.summary: Zig is a general-purpose language and toolchain with explicit memory management and C interoperability, used for native applications and cross-platform builds.
records.lifecycleNote: The Zig project's release index dates compiler release 0.17.0 to 2026-10-01.
